api_function: Authenticate a user by username and password. On successful authentication (200), returns a UserDTO containing the user profile and access control data (roles, permissions, contact and address info, enabled/secured flags, and audit timestamps). Authentication failures may return 401 (invalid credentials), 403 (account disabled or access forbidden), or 404 (user not found).
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be application/json containing two fields: username and password. Each field must be provided as a string. Both username and password are required and must be non-empty (blank or missing values will fail authentication). Username must correspond to an existing account (otherwise a 404 may be returned). Password comparison is case-sensitive; an incorrect value will yield 401. Whitespace should be avoided or trimmed to prevent mismatches. No specific length or format constraints are declared in the schema, so clients should send plain string values without additional structure. Extra fields, if sent, are not specified and may be ignored by the server.

api_function: Retrieve the user presentation list. It returns an array of user objects with profile details (name, surname, gender, birthDate), account metadata (id, username, enabled, secured, creationDt, updatedDt, loginDt), contact information (email, phone, social links, website, contactNote), address details, and assigned roles and permissions. Intended for user management/RBAC views.
parameters_constraints: This endpoint does not accept any path, query, or body parameters; clients must issue a GET request without a request body. A valid authenticated request is likely required; unauthenticated or unauthorized requests may receive 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden. No pagination or filtering parameters are defined, so additional query parameters should not be sent.

api_function: Create a new user account. The client sends a JSON payload with account credentials and optional profile/contact details. On success the server returns the created user data (UserDTO) and may respond with 200 OK (with body) or 201 Created. Requests may be rejected with 401/403 if not authorized.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be a JSON object matching the CreateOrUpdateUserDTO schema. Each field must respect its declared type/format: username: string; should be a non-empty text identifier (avoid leading/trailing spaces). password: string; should be a non-empty secret string. name and surname: strings; free text. email: string; if provided, it should be a well-formed email address (e.g., local@domain). mobile: string; if provided, it should represent a phone number (digits and optional leading '+' and separators). birthDate: string with date format (ISO 8601 calendar date, e.g., YYYY-MM-DD). enabled: boolean (true/false). secured: boolean (true/false). gender: string; free text, use a value supported by the system if such a list exists. address, address2, city, country, zipCode: strings; free-form postal information (zipCode may include letters, digits, and hyphens depending on locale). website: string; if provided, it should be a valid URL (preferably starting with http:// or https://). facebook, linkedin, skype: strings; may be profile handles or URLs; if URLs are sent, they should be valid. contactNote and note: strings; free text. All properties are optional unless your business rules require them; when supplied, their types must match the schema (no numbers/booleans where strings are expected, and booleans must be JSON true/false). Do not include unknown properties beyond those defined by the schema. Ensure date strings are valid calendar dates; email/URL/phone strings, when provided, follow their typical formats to avoid validation errors.

api_function: Retrieves the list of RBAC permission presentations available in the system. Returns an array of PermissionDTO objects, each containing an id (int64) and a permission name (string). Typically used to display or manage assignable permissions in an authentication/authorization backend.
parameters_constraints: This endpoint does not accept path, query, or body parameters. A valid Authorization credential is required: the Authorization header (e.g., a valid bearer token/session) must be present and valid; otherwise the server responds with 401 (Unauthorized). If the authenticated principal lacks sufficient privilege to list permissions, the server responds with 403 (Forbidden). Do not send a request body. The request method must be GET; the response is an array (JSON) and can be negotiated with a broad Accept header (e.g., */*).

api_function: Retrieve the list of RBAC roles available in the system, including each role's ID, name, and its associated permissions (each with ID and permission string). This is typically used to present or manage roles in an authentication/authorization backend.
parameters_constraints: This endpoint does not accept any path, query, or body parameters; the request body must be empty. A valid authenticated context is required (e.g., a valid Authorization credential) to avoid 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden responses. The request should be a GET; content negotiation is not strict (generic */* is supported).

api_function: Create a new RBAC role by posting the role name. On success, the service returns the created role descriptor (RoleDTO) including its generated id, the role name, and its permissions (initially typically empty). Appropriate authentication/authorization is required; otherwise 401/403 may be returned.
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be sent as application/json containing a single JSON string that represents the role name (for example, "Admin"). It must be a string value (not an object or array). The string should be non-empty and not only whitespace; trim leading/trailing spaces to avoid unintended names. Use a reasonable, human-readable identifier and avoid control characters; sticking to ASCII letters, digits, hyphens (-), underscores (_), and dots (.) helps prevent encoding or validation issues. Because this endpoint creates a new role, the provided name should not duplicate an existing role name; duplicate names are typically rejected with a 4xx error. No other fields are accepted in the body.

api_function: Retrieve a role (RBAC) by its ID, returning the role's basic information and its permissions. On success, the response includes the role id, role name, and a list of permissions. Requests require proper authentication/authorization (401/403 on failure), and a non-existent role id yields 404.
parameters_constraints: roleId is a required path parameter and must be a valid base‑10 integer within the signed 64‑bit range (no decimals or non‑numeric characters). It should represent a positive identifier (> 0) for an existing role; otherwise, the server responds with 404 Not Found.

api_function: Deletes an RBAC role identified by its numeric ID. This endpoint is part of the user access control system and removes the specified role, subject to authorization. On success, it may return OK (with a response object) or No Content; unauthorized or forbidden requests return 401 or 403.
parameters_constraints: roleId (path): required. Must be a valid integer in base-10 without decimals or extra characters, fitting in a 64-bit signed integer range. As an identifier, it should be a non-negative, typically strictly positive (>0) whole number and should correspond to an existing role. It must be provided as a URL path segment (e.g., /users/rbac/roles/123), not empty, and cannot contain spaces or non-numeric characters.

api_function: Adds (assigns) a permission to a role in the RBAC system. The role is identified by roleId and the permission by permissionKey. On success, it returns the updated RoleDTO (including role id, role name, and the full list of permissions). If the client is not authenticated it returns 401; if the client lacks rights it returns 403; and if the specified role or permission does not exist it returns 404. Implementations may return 200 when the association already exists or is updated, and 201 when the assignment is newly created.
parameters_constraints: roleId: required path parameter; must be a valid 64-bit signed integer (int64) expressed in digits, without decimals or signs other than an optional leading plus; should be a positive value referencing an existing role, otherwise the server will likely respond with 404; values outside the int64 range are invalid. permissionKey: required path parameter; must be a non-empty string that exactly matches a predefined permission key in the RBAC registry; it is case-sensitive and must not contain spaces or unencoded path delimiters (e.g., '/' ); if it contains reserved characters (e.g., ':', '.', '-'), they must be URL-safe or URL-encoded; an unknown key will typically result in 404.

api_function: Remove a specific permission from a role in the RBAC system. Given a role ID and a permission key, this endpoint detaches that permission from the role. On success it may return the updated role (with its remaining permissions) in a 200 response, or no body in a 204 response. Requests require valid authentication and authorization; unauthorized or forbidden access yields 401/403.
parameters_constraints: Both path parameters are required and cannot be null or empty. roleId: must be a 64-bit signed integer (int64) represented as a positive whole number in the URL (digits only, no decimals, signs, or whitespace). It must correspond to an existing role for the removal to succeed. permissionKey: must be a non-empty string that exactly matches an existing permission key defined by the system (case-sensitive). As a path segment, it must be URI-safe: it cannot contain '/' and any reserved/special characters must be percent-encoded; avoid leading/trailing spaces. If permissionKey does not correspond to a valid permission identifier, the operation will not succeed.

api_function: Create (register) a new user account in the authentication/authorization service. The client submits a RegisterUserAccountDTO (username, password, email, name, surname, gender) and, on success, the service creates the account and returns the created user's profile (UserDTO) or indicates creation. This endpoint is part of user management/RBAC and may enforce access control (401/403).
parameters_constraints: The request body is required and must be application/json containing a JSON object with the fields email, gender, name, password, surname, and username (all strings). At minimum, username and password should be provided as non-empty strings to enable authentication. Username must be a valid account identifier and is typically unique within the system; avoid leading/trailing whitespace and control characters, and use a reasonable length and character set (e.g., letters, digits, underscores, dots). Password must be a non-empty string that satisfies the system’s password policy (e.g., minimum length and complexity such as a mix of character types). Email should be a syntactically valid email address (RFC-compliant) and is commonly treated as case-insensitive; many systems also require it to be unique. Name and surname are free-text strings; if provided, they should be human-readable, trimmed (no leading/trailing spaces), and within a reasonable length; avoid control characters. Gender, if provided, should match one of the backend’s accepted values (e.g., MALE/FEMALE/OTHER or similar), rather than an arbitrary phrase, and is case-sensitive depending on implementation. Fields not defined in the schema may be ignored or rejected; null values are generally not acceptable for string fields—omit optional fields instead of sending null. Ensure the Content-Type header is application/json.

api_function: Retrieve a user's full details by their unique identifier. On success, returns a UserDTO containing profile information (name, surname, username, gender, birthDate), contact and address data, account flags (enabled, secured), roles and permissions, and timestamps (creationDt, updatedDt, loginDt). Typical auth/authorization applies (401/403), and a non-existent user yields 404.
parameters_constraints: Path parameter id is required and must be a 64-bit signed integer (int64). Provide it as a whole number embedded in the URL path (e.g., /users/123). It must contain only digits (no decimals, separators, or whitespace), fit within the int64 range, and typically be a positive value. If the id does not correspond to an existing user, the request will result in 404; malformed or non-integer values will not be accepted by the path binding.

api_function: Update an existing user's account by ID. The endpoint accepts a JSON payload containing profile, contact, login, and status fields (e.g., name, surname, username, email, password, birthDate, enabled, secured, address/contact details) and returns the updated user representation. In an RBAC-oriented user management service, this is used to maintain user profiles and access-related flags. The server may return 200 for a successful update or 201 if a resource is created as a result of the operation.
parameters_constraints: The path parameter id is required and must be a 64-bit integer (int64); it should be a positive whole number corresponding to an existing user (nonexistent IDs may yield 404). The request body is required and must be application/json with an object payload. Field constraints by type/format: birthDate must be a string formatted as a calendar date (ISO 8601, YYYY-MM-DD) with no time component. enabled and secured must be boolean values (true or false). email should be a syntactically valid email address string. All other listed fields (address, address2, city, contactNote, country, facebook, gender, linkedin, mobile, name, note, password, skype, surname, username, website, zipCode) are strings with no explicit format or length constraints defined in the schema; if provided, they should be non-empty text appropriate to their semantics. Content-Type must be application/json, and only defined fields should be included; unspecified fields are optional and may be omitted.

api_function: Delete a user account by its unique numeric identifier. This endpoint is part of the user management/RBAC service and typically requires authentication and sufficient permissions. On successful deletion it may return OK (200) or No Content (204); unauthorized or forbidden access yields 401/403.
parameters_constraints: Path parameter id is required and must be a whole number that fits a 64-bit signed integer (int64). It should be provided as a non-empty path segment containing only digits (no decimals or non-numeric characters) and, in typical systems, be a positive integer greater than 0. The value must correspond to an existing user record for the deletion to take effect.

api_function: Assigns (adds) a role to a user in the RBAC system. Given a user ID and a role ID in the path, the API links the specified role to the user and returns the updated user representation (UserDTO) including roles, permissions, and profile fields.
parameters_constraints: id: required path parameter; must be a signed 64-bit integer (int64) provided in the URL path; should be a positive whole number and represent an existing user. Non-integer values, decimals, scientific notation, empty/omitted values, or values outside the int64 range are invalid; if the referenced user does not exist, a 404 may be returned. roleId: required path parameter; must be a signed 64-bit integer (int64) provided in the URL path; should be a positive whole number and represent an existing role. Non-integer values, decimals, scientific notation, empty/omitted values, or values outside the int64 range are invalid; if the referenced role does not exist, a 404 may be returned. No request body is expected for this operation; both parameters must be supplied in the path.

api_function: Remove a specific role assignment from a given user. This RBAC management endpoint dissociates the role identified by roleId from the user identified by id. On success it may return the updated UserDTO (200 OK) or no body (204 No Content). Requests require proper authorization (401/403 on failure).
parameters_constraints: Both path parameters are required and must be integers (int64) encoded in the URL path. The parameter id must be a valid 64-bit signed integer identifying an existing user (typically a positive, non-zero numeric ID; no decimals or non-numeric characters). The parameter roleId must be a valid 64-bit signed integer identifying an existing role (typically a positive, non-zero numeric ID; no decimals or non-numeric characters). Neither parameter can be omitted or null since they are path variables, and they must fit within the 64-bit signed integer range.
